meaning: The number 50,000 has no well-established independent symbolic meaning in biblical tradition, but appears in several biblical contexts related to magnitude, strength, and purification.
description: Although the number 50 has strong symbolic meaning linked to jubilee, freedom and the Holy Spirit (Pentecost/Shavuot falls on the 50th day after Easter), the specific number 50000 does not have an acknowledged symbolic role in biblical or Jewish tradition. The number nevertheless appears in several biblical texts. In 1 Chronicles 5:21, 50000 camels are taken as war booty after a victory God gave, and in 1 Chronicles 12:34, 50000 men from Zebulun are described as standing up with "an undivided heart" to make David king. In Acts 19:19, new converts in Ephesus burned magic books worth 50000 silver coins – a dramatic expression of spiritual cleansing and reckoning with idolatry. Any interpretations of 50000 would typically be based on the combination of the numbers 50 and 1000, where both represent completeness and divine abundance, but such combined interpretations do not have broad support in traditional sources.

versions.reason: [major] The description mentions only 1 Samuel 6:19 (which moreover states 50,070, not 50,000) but overlooks the actual Bible verses where 50,000 appears: 1 Chronicles 5:21, 1 Chronicles 12:34, and Acts 19:19. These provide a better basis for discussing the number.; [major] The reference to 1 Samuel 6:19 with the number 50,070 is misleading because it is not the number 50,000. The actual occurrences of 50,000 should be used instead.; [minor] The description could better make use of the actual biblical occurrences to illuminate contexts where 50,000 appears – such as war spoils, military strength, and spiritual cleansing – without overstating symbolic meaning.; [minor] Interesting details about the biblical occurrences (especially Acts 19:19 and 1 Chronicles 12:34) fit well as footnotes to enrich the content.

footnotes.text: In 1 Chronicles 12:34, the expression "undivided heart" (Hebrew: lo lev va-lev, literally "not with two hearts") is used regarding Zebulun's 50,000 warriors—a formulation that emphasizes complete loyalty and devotion to David's kingdom.

The value of 50,000 silver coins (Greek: arguriou muriadas pente) in Acts 19:19 represented an enormous sum, estimated at 50,000 days' wages. Luke uses this number to highlight the scale of spiritual conversion in Ephesus and the grip of magic on the city.

Some rabbinic commentators view large, rounded numbers in the Bible as expressions of divine abundance rather than exact quantities. In this tradition, 50,000—as a product of the Jubilee number 50 and the complete thousand—would reinforce the impression of God's rich blessing.
